newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss rule out apology for blackmail remarks.
newsitem.headline: Swiss rule out apology for blackmail remarks.

text.p: Swiss President Arnold Koller said the government was not planning to apologise for remarks by his predecessor Jean-Pascal Delamuraz, who described calls for Swiss restitution to Holocaust victims as blackmail.

He told Swiss-German television late on Friday that Delamuraz had already publically expressed regret for his remarks, which angered Jewish groups and triggered threats of a boycott against Swiss banks.
"A further distancing is not being discussed," Koller said in the Arena television programme.
Delamuraz's remarks reignited a dispute between Switzerland and Jewish groups over how to investigate the fate of Jewish funds deposited in Swiss banks before and up to World War Two.
While the Swiss government has ignored demands that it denounce the remarks, Koller said it was willing to discuss setting up a Holocaust memorial fund with banks.
This move should not be viewed as the government giving in to any pressure, Koller added.
The government has already acknowledged that it might compensate Jewish victims of the Nazis before the final results of a full inquiry -- which could take years -- was completed.

Swiss Jews groups have proposed that the government repay Jewish groups the 55 million Swiss francs ($40 million) they spent to support Jews who were allowed to enter Switzerland during the war. No other refugees had to pay for their own upkeep.
Delamuraz made his remarks last month as he completed his one-year term in the rotating Swiss presidency.
The remarks triggered angry reactions not only from outraged Israeli politicians and world Jewish groups, but also from other Swiss politicians.
On Friday the Social Democrats, one of four parties in the centre-left coalition that has ruled since 1959, said the council must distance itself from Delamuraz's remarks.
"These comments are not only an unbearable insult to victims of the Holocaust. They also insult Switzerland and the Swiss people at the same time," it said.

Groups led by the World Jewish Congress (WJC) say Swiss banks and government profited cynically from the Holocaust by sitting on accounts left ownerless by Jewish victims and by buying stolen gold from Nazi Germany during World War Two. ($1=1.3713 Swiss Franc)
